O.I.H.  
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2209 
  ANSWERED ON 20/12/2022 
 
RELEASE OF FUNDS UNDER MGNREGS 
 
2209.  SHRI ARJUN LAL MEENA: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to release funds to the State of Rajasthan under 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) and 
provide necessary options for payment of material and administrative items in the 
MGNREGS soft portal; and 
(b)  if so, the time by which it is likely to be done and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) & (b):  Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment Scheme.  
 
Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, States/UTs (including Rajasthan)  furnish funds 
release proposals to the Government of India. The Ministry releases funds periodically in two 
tranches with each tranche consisting of one or more installments, keeping in view the 
“agreed to” Labour Budget, demand for works, opening balance, pace of utilization of funds, 
pending liabilities, overall per formance and subject to submission of relevant documents by 
the States/UTs. 
 
Fund release to the States/UTs is a continuous process and Central Government is 
committed in making funds available to States/UTs for the implementation of the Scheme as 
per the demand for work on the ground.  
 
In current financial year 2022-23, (as on 16.12.2022), an amount of Rs. 4,259.03 crore 
has been released for wage component and an amount of Rs.1,900 core has been released for 
material and administrative components to the State of Rajasthan under Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS.  
  
Wage payment is directly released into the accounts of beneficiaries through Direct 
Benefit Transfer (DBT) and funds for material and administrative components are released to 
the State Treasury under the Scheme.  
 
 
*******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2210 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 20th DECEMBER, 2022 
 
FODDER CENTRIC FARMER PRODUCER ORGANISATION 
 
2210. SHRI KULDEEP RAI SHARMA:  
SHRI B.B. PATIL: 
 DR. SUBHASH RAMRAO BHAMRE:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the wholesale price index based fodder inflation soared to a nine year high of 25.5 
percent in August, 2022 and if so, whether this has resulted in hardship to rural families 
whose livelihood are dependent on livestock; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the current availability of fodder and the na ture of 
shortage and its adverse impact on the dairy product;  
(c) if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether the Government has proposed the formation and promotion of fodder -centric 
Farmer Producer Organization (FPOs) to address the fodder deficit and has planned to set up 
100 fodder centric FPOs in 2022 -23 and if so, the manner in which the proposed FPOs will 
address the problem of fodder deficit;  
(e) whether the Government has appointed implementing agency and also fixed target for the 
purpose and if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) the other steps/measures taken by the Government to promote dairy and livestock industry 
in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) Wholesale price index (WPI) data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry, 
showed that the index value for fodder has recorded at 225.7 in November 2022, 
registering an increase of 27.66 per cent over the same month last year (176.8). As such , 
no severe hardship s to rural families whose livelihood are dependent on livestock have 
reported by the States, although there is increase in the price of fodder. 
 

(b) & (c) The ICAR - Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi has 
estimated that there is deficit of 11.24 %, 23.4 % and 28.9% in green fodder, dry fodder 
and concentrates respectively at the national level. The State Governments are primarily 
responsible for assessing the shortage of fodder , if any , and its impact on the dairy 
products.As such , no reports ha ve been received by the Centre from any of the State 
Governments for any adverse impact on the dairy product during the various review 
meetings conducted by the Centre. 
 
(d) & (e) Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare has designated National Dairy 
Development Board (NDDB) as implementing agency under the scheme of Formation 
and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer organizations (FPOs) to form and promote 100 
FPOs, primarily fod der centric and animal husbandry activities as a secondary activity 
(Fodder plus model) on 04 November 2022.These Fodder Plus FPOs would engage in 
fodder development activities such as green fodder/silage production and sale, production 
of ‘ready-to-eat’ TMR, securing crop residues & its sale and also take up other animal 
husbandry activities , thereby providing market access to small and marginal farmers. 
Dairy cooperatives and other Agencies would be identified as Cluster Based Business 
Organizations (CBBO s) which would facilitate forward linkage for the produce of the 
FPOs and support the FPOs in a sustainable manner.NDDB has already initiated 
consultations with stakeholders for identification of the Milk Unions/Federations/ Milk 
Producer Organisations/Gov ernment Agencies etc. as Cluster Based Business 
Organizations (CBBOs). So far, 34 organizations have already submitted Letter of Intent 
(LoI) for formation of 62 FPOs which are being assessed. 
 
(f) Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying,  Government of India is implementing 
following schemes to supplement the efforts of the States/UTs for promotion and 
development of the animal husbandry and  dairying sector across the country, as given 
below: 
i. RashtriyaGokul Mission, 
ii. National Programme for Dairy Development, 
iii. Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund, 
iv. Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer Producer engaged in dairy      
ActivitiesOrganizations 
v. National Livestock Mission, 
vi. Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund 
vii. Livestock Health and Disease Control 
viii. National Animal Disease Control Programme 
ix. Livestock Census and Integrated Sample Survey 
 
*******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2211                                                                                                                                                                              
(TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.12.2022) 
 
DEDICATED CHANNELS FOR FARMERS 
 
2211. SHRI JUAL ORAM: 
  
        Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the details of initiatives taken by the Government towards 
educating the farmers through Radio/TV;  
 
(b) whether the Government is operating any dedicated channels for 
this purpose, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) the funds allocated and utilized on running such dedicated 
channels so far?   
 
  

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING ; AND 
MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  (SHRI ANURAG SINGH 
THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b):  Prasar Bharati telecasts “DD Kisan”, a 24X7 satellite TV 
channel, exclusively dedicated to the farmers and the agriculture 
sector. DD Kisan was launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri 
Narendra Modi, on 26th May, 2015. The objective of this channel is 
to serve the farming and rural community in India and to reach the 
remotest parts of the country, to inform and educate the rural 
populace and work towards creating a holistic environment for 
sustainable and inclusive growth of the farmers. DD Kisan channel is 
also streamed LIVE on “YouTube” and all programmes are uploaded 
on YouTube after telecast for off line viewing. 
In addition, Prasar Bharati broadcasts a 30 minute, six days a week, 
dedicated interactive programme “Kisanvani” in respective regional 
languages in over 96 All India Radio (AIR) stations across the 
country and “Kisan  Ki  Baat”  programme  over  FM  Gold Channel in 
Delhi, for the farming community in collaboration  with Ministry of 
Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Further,  
programmes towards educating farmers on various aspects are also 
being carried on AIR and DD Network across the country. 
(c): From year 2014 -15 upto November, 2022, total fund allocated 
and utilized for DD Kisan  is Rs.318.64 crore and Rs.264.72 crore 
respectively.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2214 
ANSWERED ON 20TH DECEMBER, 2022  
  
 PMFME SCHEME 
2214. DR. VISHNU PRASAD M.K.: 
  
          Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a)  the number of States in which the PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises 
(PMFME) Scheme has been implemented so far; 
 
(b)  the details of the successful outcome of the said scheme; 
 
(c)  the amount of subsidy released in the country including Tamil Nadu under the said scheme 
during the last two years and the current year; and 
 
(d)  the details of steps being taken to make the said scheme more transparent?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
  
(a). 35 States/UTs are implementing PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises 
(PMFME) Scheme in the country. West Bengal is yet to decide on participation in the scheme. 
 
(b). The details of outcome / achievements made under the Scheme till date, since its inception are 
at Annexure-I.  
 
(c). The amount of subsidy released in the country including Tamil Nadu  under the PMFME 
schemes during the last two years (till date) is at Annexure-II.  
 
(d).  To implement the scheme in transparent manner, an institutional mechanism has been kept in 
place at National, State and District levels.  At the national level, Inter -Ministerial Empowered 
Committee (IMEC) has been constituted as a policy making body to give overall direction, guidance 
for implementation of the scheme and monitor & review its progress and performance. Further, all 
the States/ UTs have appointed State Nodal Agencies (SNAs), constituted State Level Approval 
Committees (SLACs) & District Level Committees (DLCs) for implementation of the scheme.  
Online portal has also been in place for submission of applications, approval and release of subsidy 
under the scheme. 
 
 
***** 

  Annexure-I 
 
ANNEXURE REFERRED IN REPLY TO PART (b) OF THE LOK SABHA UNSTARRED 
QUESTION NO. 2214 FOR ANSWER ON 2 0.12.2022 REGARDING  
“PMFME SCHEME” 
Details of outcome / achievements made under the Scheme till date 
 
1. All the States/ UTs have appointed State Nodal Agency  (SNA), consti tuted State Level  
Approval C ommittee (SLAC) & District Level Committee  (DLC) for implementation of the 
scheme. The Government of West Bengal is yet to decide on participation in the scheme. 
 
2. 35 States/ UTs have nominated 42 State Level Technical Institutions (SLTI) which has been 
approved by the Ministry. 
 
3. 35 States/ UTs recommended ODOPs for 713 districts which has been approved by the 
Ministry. 
 
4. 55,357 applications of individual micro food processing enterprises have been submitted 
for Credit linked subsidy out of which 12,561 loans sanctioned and Grant in Aid - Center Share 
released to 4,667 beneficiaries amounting to Rs. 110.86 crore. 
 
5. Seed capital amount of Rs. 308.58 crores released to 95,852 SHG members. 
 
6. 76 Incubation Centres has been approved with an outlay of Rs. 205.95 cr. for establishment 
of Incubation Centre which are established in ODOP processing lines and allied product lines. 
 
7. 2 National Tie-ups with NAFED has been done and 12 brands have been launched under 
the scheme. 6 State proposals have been approved  which include Punjab (Aasna), Maharashtra 
(Bhimthadi), Karnataka (Seemi and Bhima) and Andhra Pradesh (Madugula Halwa and 
Aamodam). 
 
8. 487 Master Trainers of 35 States/UTs trained; 843 District Level Trainers trained on ODOP 
and EDP. 9,036 beneficiaries trained so far. 
 
9. 1736 District Resource Persons (DRPs) appointed in 35 States/UTs. 
 
10. NIFTEMs have prepared training modules (ODOP) which have been published on MOFPI 
and NIFTEMs website. These include 760 training modules (ODOP) which include 190 
Presentations, 190 Videos, 190 DPRs and 190 Course Content/Handbooks 
 
11. MoFPI has signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) / Joint Letters with Department 
of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Indian Council for Agriculture Research (ICAR), 
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Food Safety and Standards Authority of 
India (FSSAI), Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs 
(MoHUA), Ministry of Tribal Affairs, National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC ), 
National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) and National 
Schedule Finance Development Corporation (NSFDC) apart from many other Government 
Institutions for convergence of PMFME with other schemes, identification & handholding of 
beneficiaries, support in capacity building, marketing & branding and increasing outreach of 
scheme.

DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2215 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20TH DECEMBER, 2022 
 
Fish Farming and Cow Rearing 
 
2215.        SHRI RAMDAS C. TADAS:  
 
 Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING, 
मत्स्यपालन पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has formulated or proposed to formulate any action plan to 
promote fish farming and cow rearing in the country; 
(b) whether the Government has decided to implement any scheme in Maharashtra 
keeping in view the potential of fish farming in the State; and 
(c)     if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) to (c): To complement and supplement the efforts of the States/UTs for promotion of 
fisheries and Animal Husbandry sectors including cow rearing, the Ministry of Fisheries, 
Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India implement various schemes across the 
country including Maharashtra, such as (i) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY), (ii) Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), (iii) 
National Programme for Dai ry Development (NPDD), (iv) Dairy Processing and 
Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF), (v) Supporting Dairy Cooperative and Farmer 
Producer Organizations (FPO) engaged in dairy activities, (vi) Dairy Entrepreneurship 
Development Scheme (DEDS) , (vii) Anim al Husbandry Infrastructur e Development Fund 
(AHIDF), etc.   
 
The Department of Fisheries has approved project proposal at a total outlay of 
Rs.607.73 crores with Central share of Rs .239.57 crores for development of fisheries and 
aquaculture in the State of Maharashtra under PMMSY since its inception in 2020 -21. The 
major activities approved under the PMMSY inter-alia includes construction of ponds  for 
taking up of aquaculture activities including i nputs support in both Inland and Brackish  
water, installation of cages/  pens for fish culture in reservoirs and open water bodies, 
integrated development of reservoirs, establishment of hatchery, construction of seed rearing 
area,  promotion  of  seaweed  cultivation, Marine  Cage  culture  and  bi-valve  culture,  
 

 
establishment of Re -circulatory Aquaculture System (RAS) establishment fish feed mill, 
development of post harvest infrastructure such as ice plants, cold storages, ice plants -cum-
cold storages fish transportation and marketing infrastructures such as refrigerated and 
insulated vehicles, Ice-box with two/three wheelers, live fish vending units, fish kiosks, etc.  
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing  Rashtriya Gokul 
Mission for development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds since  December 
2014. The scheme is important in enhancing milk production and productivity of bovines to 
meet growing demand of milk and making dairying more remunerative to the rural farmers of 
the country. The scheme is continued under revised and realigned form for a period of 5 years 
from 2021-22 to 2025-26 with an allocation of Rs.2400 crore s. The scheme aims to enhance 
productivity and create benefits to 80 million farmers engaged in dairying especially small 
and marginal farmers.

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Youth Affairs 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2219 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.12.2022 
 
Strengthening of NYKS 
 
2219. SHRI MANOJ KOTAK: 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government is strengthening Nehru 
Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS), which is having its presence in 623 
districts in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof especially for Maharashtra; 
(c) whether the Government has any plan to open more NYKS in the 
country and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has provided any special funds to North-
Eastern States for NYKS; and 
(e) if so, the details of funds provided during the last three years? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR] 
(a) & (b) Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan(NYKS) is an autonomous body 
under the Ministry, established with the objective of providing rural 
youth avenues to take part in the process of nation building as well as 
providing opportunities for the development of their personality and 
skills. Strengthening of Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan(NYKS) is an 

ongoing process. NYKS at present has presence in 623 districts 
across the country including 34 districts in the state of Maharashtra 
out of its 36 districts. The core strength of NYKS lies in its network of 
youth clubs. Over the years, Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan has 
established a wide network of rural/urban youth clubs. It channelizes 
the power of youth on the principles of voluntarism, self-help and 
community participation. The youth have been given opportunity to 
participate in NYKS core programs like training on youth leadership & 
community development, Block and District level sports meet, 
information on basic vocations & soft skills, District level promotion of 
folk art, cultural programs & Yuva Kriti, District Youth Conventions, 
Declamation contests, Swachhata Awareness & Shramdaan, Training 
on clean village-green village and also to participate in adventure 
camps, National Integration Camps, Lifeskill Education, Inter-state 
Youth Exchange Programs( Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat) and Tribal 
Youth Exchange Program supported by Ministry of Home Affairs etc. 
These programs enable to enhance the leadership qualities of the 
youth and encourage them to participate in Nation building activities. 
(c) There is no plan under consideration to open more NYKs in the 
country as of now. 
(d) & (e) NYKS releases funds to all its State Offices including NE 
States for conduct of its regular program as per the Annual Action 
Plan. Funds for NE states are not earmarked separately.

2220.  SHRIMATI JASKAUR MEENA: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the salient features of the National Rural Livelihood Mission; 
(b)  the details of funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized under this mission during the 
last three years in Rajasthan; 
(c)  the details of the target set and the achievements made so far under the mission in the 
country; 
(d)  whether the Government has formulated a specific strategy under this mission to 
cover the poor rural women which were not included in Self Help Groups; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY -NRLM) 
is an anti-poverty programme which aims at organising the rural poor women into Self Help 
Groups (SHGs) and their federations and facilitating them to access credit from Banks and 
also in taking up various livelihoods activities for enhancing their incomes. The programme 
is being implemented in all the States and Union Territories, except Delhi and Chandigarh.  
 The salient features of the DAY-NRLM are as follows: 
i. Promotion of Sustainable Institutions of the poor 
ii. Ensuring access to financial services 
iii. Promote diversified livelihoods opportunities for the poor, in farm and non- farm 
sectors. 
iv. Promotion of Skill Development and access to wage wmployment 
v. Promotion of Social Inclusion and Human Development                  . 
  
(b) The details of the funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized under this mission during 
the last three years in Rajasthan are provided in the table below:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2224 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20TH DECEMBER, 2022 
 
Subsidised Kerosene for Fishing Sector 
 
2224.  SHRI K. MURALEEDHARAN: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has noted that over the years, the quantity of subsidised kerosene for the 
fishing sector in Kerala has dipped and the requirement of the fishing sector in Kerala is around 
20,000 kl per month, but it receives around 12,000 kl and in  the traditional sector, boats 
deploying engines with power up to 9.9 hp are eligible for 129 litres of subsidised kerosene per 
month but not even a tenth of supplies are being received;  
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Government has taken any step to mitigate the situation; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)  
(a)  and (b):  The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has informed that the Government of India makes 
allocation of Public Distribution System (PDS) Kerosene to States/UTs on quarterly basis for cooking and 
lighting purpose. PDS allocation to States/UTs have been rationalized since 2010 -11 taking into account, 
factors such as incr ease in domestic LPG/PNG connections, electricity coverage, non -lifting of PDS 
Kerosene quota by concerned States/UTs etc. 
 Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has further informed that the Government vide order 
dated 21 st August, 2012 has empowered States /UTs to draw an allocation of one month’s quota of PDS 
Kerosene at Non -subsidized rates during each financial year for special needs such as natural calamities, 
religious functions, fisheries, various yatras etc. Annual allocation of Non -Subsidized PDS Ker osene is 
done by Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC) in the beginning of each financial year. States/UTs 
may seek further additional allocation after exhausting available quota. 
 (c) and (d):  The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has informed that  considering the request of 
Government of Kerala, in addition to already allocated quota of 2160 KL, additional allocation of Non -
Subsidized PDS Kerosene has been done making an overall allocation of 7160 KL non subsidized PDS 
SKO for year 2022 -23. Also, for the FY 2022 -23 an allocation of 15552 KL Subsidized PDS kerosene has 
been made to the state of Kerala.

COOPERATIVE MILK PRODUCTION CENTRES 
 
2225. SHRIMATI VEENA DEVI: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has worked any plan to provide loans to the farmers at cheaper rate to 
increase milk productivity, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the total number of cooperative milk production centres in the country, State -wise including 
Uttar Pradesh; 
(c) the details of policy to improve the condition of these centres; 
(d) whether the Government has formulated any concrete policy to provide cheaper loans for the 
purchase of livestock and to promote the dairy sector; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 (SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) and (d) Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing the following schemes 
for providing subsidy and interest subvention to the farmers to increase milk productivity 
  
(i)   One of the components of the scheme Rashtriya Gokul Mission is to promote establishme nt of 
breed multiplication farm on hub and spoke model. Under the scheme 50% capital subsidy 
maximum up to Rs.2.00 crore is available for eligible entrepreneurs. Entrepreneurs assisted under 
establishment of breed multiplication farm are also eligible for interest subvention under Animal 
Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund.  
 
(ii) Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) - This scheme is being 
implemented with the objective of creation/ strengthening of milk processing, v alue additio n & 
chilling facilities. Under the scheme, NABARD raises the fund from market  and disburse loan to 
dairy cooperatives with 2.5% interest subvention through National Dairy Development Board and 

National Cooperative Development Corporation. Department of Ani mal Husbandry and Dairying 
provides 2.5% interest subvention to National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. 
 
(iii)  Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) – under the scheme 3% 
interest subvention is made available to eligible beneficiaries availing for establishment of dairy 
processing and value addition infrastructure in addition to other components of the scheme. 
 
 (iv) Support to State Dairy Cooperative & Farmers Producers Organization (SDCFPO): under 
the scheme one time sup port in the form of Interest sub vention on working capital loan  has been 
introduced from the financial year 2020-21. 
 
(v)        Kisan Credit Card (KCC) – For the first time, Government of India has extended KCC 
facility to Animal Husbandry and Fisheries f armers for their working capital requirement wherein 
farmers either individual or joint borrower, Joint Liability Groups or Self Help Groups including 
tenant farmers having owned/rented/leased sheds are eligible for getting benefits under the 
scheme. 
 
(b) The total number of cooperative milk production centres in the country, State -wise including 
Uttar Pradesh is given at Annexure I  
 
(c) and (e)   Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing the following 
schemes to improve the condition of c ooperative milk production centres: (i) National Programme 
for Dairy Development ; (ii) Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund and (iii) Support to Dairy 
Cooperative and Farmer Producers’ Organisations.

  ANSWERED ON 20/12/2022 
 
MERGER OF DRDA 
2226.  SHRI G.M. SIDDESHWAR: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether any policy has been prepared for the merger of District Rural Development 
Agencies with Zilla Parishads in order to strengthen the Panchayati Raj; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the purposes it is supposed to fulfill; 
(c)  whether the policy also envisages the proposal to absorb the employees of District 
Rural Development Agencies in Zilla Parishads; and 
(d)  the number of States where District Rural Development Agencies have been merged 
with Zilla Parishads? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (c)  The Government had decided to discontinue District Rural Development Agencies  
(DRDA) with effect from 01.04.2022 and this decision has been communicated to States/UTs 
with the request to take the following actions :- 
  
(i) The States/UTs   may merge the DRDAs with the 
ZillaParishad/ZilaPanchayats of the States/UTs. Where there are no ZPs e.g. in 
North Eastern States, the DRDA may be merged with District Counci ls or any 
other body, as may be decided by the State Government; 
  
(ii) Staff working at the DRDAs on deputation basis can be absorbed back in 
their parent departments; 
  
(iii) The support staff who are on the rolls of the DRDAs may be absorbed     (a) 
by the appropriate line departments; 
(b) in the District Planning and Monitoring Body as per their qualification. In 
case such fitment is not possible and is not organic, they can be placed with other 
schemes as per their competencies and qualifications in suitable capacities; 
  
(iv) The accounts of funds released under DRDA scheme may be got audited and 
the balance/ unutilized amount with DRDAs as on 31.03.2022 reflected in Audit 
Reports, may be transferred to Zila Panchayats/ Zila Council or any other body, 
as the case may be and be accounted for in subsequent releases. 
   
(d)   As per available information,    three States Government (namely Uttar Pradesh, 
Madhya Pradesh and Odisha)  have merged their District Rural Development Agencies with 
Zilla Parishad/ Zila Panchayat/Others Bodies.

Cooperative System 
 
2231: SHRI HANUMAN BENIWAL: 
 SHRI POCHA BRAHMANANDA REDDY 
 
Will the Minister of Cooperation (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state:  
 
a) The number of registered cooperatives in the country, State-wise; 
b) The details of the benefits and incentives given to registered cooperatives; 
c) whether the Government has taken any steps to increase cooperative registrations in 
the country, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons thereof; 
d) the funds sanctioned and released, State-wise, for the welfare of cooperatives in the 
country; and  
e) The details of steps taken by the Government to strengthen co-operative system in the 
country during the last five years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION  
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (e): There are about 8.54 lakh cooperatives in the country as per Statistical Profile-2018 
published by National Cooperative Union of India. State-wise and sector-wise distribution of 
cooperative societies is enclosed at Annexure-I. Cooperative Sector plays a key role in the 
overall economic development of the country with its member driven approach. The 
Cooperative Societies with objects confined to one State are governed under the respective 
State Cooperative Societies Act, whereas the Cooperative Societies with objects not confined 
to one State are administered under the provisions of Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act 
(MSCS), 2002 and rules made there under. There are 1528 cooperative societies registered 
under MSCS Act, 2002. Details of multi state cooperative societies registered under the 
MSCS Act, 2002 in the last three years are as under: 
 
Sl. No. Year No. of Societies 
1. 2020 10 
2. 2021 14 
3. 2022 
 (up to 30th November, 2022) 
63 
 Total 87 
 
In order to strengthen co-operative systemand deepening its reach to the grassroots in 
the country, the Ministry of Cooperation has taken various initiatives such as: 

i. Project for Computerization of 63,000 functional Primary Agriculture Credit Societies 
(PACS), in next three years, with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore has been 
approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs vide its decision dated 29th 
June, 2022. This project entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP 
(Enterprise Resource Planning) based common software, linking them with NABARD 
through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks 
(DCCBs).  
ii. Model bye laws for PACS have been prepared after detailed stakeholder 
consultations, including all the States/ Union Territories and Ministries concerned, for 
adoption by PACS as per their respective State Cooperatives Societies Act. These 
Model Byelaws of PACS will enable them to undertake more than 25 business 
activities like dairy, fishery, floriculture, setting up of godowns, procurement of 
foodgrains, fertilizers, seeds, LPG/ Petrol/ Green energy distribution agency, banking 
correspondents, common service centres, etc. 
iii. On 1st June, 2022, Union Cabinet has taken a decision allowing cooperatives to 
register as ‘buyer’ on Government e-Marketing platform, enabling them to procure 
goods and services from nearly 40 lakh vendors registered on the GeM portal 
throughout the country. This will help cooperatives in making savings and improving 
transparency in their procurement system. 
iv. Surcharge on Co-operative societies was reduced from 12 % to 7% for those co-
operative societies having a total income of more than Rs. 1 Cr. and up to Rs. 10 Cr. 
to enhance the income of Co-operative societies and its members. 
v. Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) rate reduced for the Co-operatives from 18.5% to 
15% to provide them a level playing field with Corporates. 
vi. In order to provide adequate, affordable and timely credit to the co-operative 
institutions to give a boost to the co-operative based economic development model, 
non-scheduled Urban Co-operative Banks, State Co-operative Banks and District 
Central Co-operative Banks have been notified as Member Lending Institutions in 
Guarantee Fund Trust (CGTMSE) Scheme vide circular dated 3rd February, 2022. 
vii. Government vide its notification dated 25th October, 2021 offered a major relief to 
co-operative sugar mills by clarifying that sugar co-operative mills shall not be 
subjected to additional income tax for paying higher sugarcane prices to farmers upto 
to the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) or State Advised Price (SAP), as the case 
may be. 
viii. National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization 
under the Ministry of Cooperation, provides financial assistance to the cooperative 
sector and undertakes various activities such as strengthening share capital base of 
primary/ District cooperative marketing societies, setting up of processing centres, 
storage facilities, establishing and modernizing cold chain, creation of cooperative 
banking units, agricultural services, Integrated Cooperative Development Projects, 
assistance for computerization of cooperatives, ‘Yuva-Sahkar’ for cooperative 
enterprise support and innovation, ‘Ayushman Sahkar’ covering healthcare sector, 
‘Nandini Sahkar’ to support women cooperatives etc.  
The details of funds sanctioned and released for the welfare of cooperatives in the 
country, State-wise, by National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) during the 
period from 01.04.2017 to 14.12.2022 is enclosed at Annexure II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2232 
ANSWERED ON 20.12. 2022 
 
SEAFOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRY 
 
2232. SHRIMATI POONAMBEN MAADAM:1067.  SHRI P. WILSON 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) whether the Government is taking steps to improve Seafood Processing Industry infrastructure 
in the country; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the number of registered seafood processing facilities that have been developed during the  
last two years;  
 
(d) whether the Government is providing special assistance to the seafood processing industry to 
tide over the crisis caused by Covid-19; and  
 
(e) if so, the financial outlay for sea food processing enterprises across the country during the last 
five years from 2020-21 to 2024-25? 
 
   
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing an umbrella 
scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) since 2017 -18 across the country. 
PMKSY is a comprehensive package of sub -schemes, aimed at creation of modern infrastructure 
with efficient supply chain management from farm gate to retail outlet. Under the following sub-
schemes of PMKSY, financial support in the form of grants-in-aid is provided for setting up projects 
including seafood processing industry: 
 
(i) Mega Food Parks Scheme (MFP) (discontinued w.e.f. 01.04.2021)  
(ii) Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition infrastructure (Cold Chain)  
(iii) Creation/ Expansion of Food Processing And Preservation Capacities (CEFPPC) 
(iv) Creation of Infrastructure Development for Agro Processing Cluster (APC) 
(v) Creation of Backward and Forward Linkages (CBFL) (discontinued w.e.f. 01.04.2021) 
 

The number of seafood processing projects approved till 12.12.2022 under various schemes of 
MoFPI is at Annexure. 
 
(c): As per the latest Annual Survey of Industries released by Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation, number of registered seafood processing units for the years 2018-19 and 2019-20 
under the category Processing and preserving of fish, crustaceans and molluscs and products 
thereof (NIC code 1020) are 593 and 654 respectively. 
 
(d) & (e): Though MoFPI has no specific schemes to provide special assistance to seafood processing 
industries to tide over the crisis caused by Covid-19, MoFPI has, in case of delays in implementation 
of projects under PMKSY,  waived off penalty for the period from 25.03.2020 to 31.05.2020 and 
from 15.04.2021 to 14.06.2021 on account of Covid -19. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of 
Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) with an estimated investment of Rs. 20050 crore for a period of five years from 
2020-21 to 2024 -25 as a part of Atma Nirbhar Package during Covid -19 pandemic. Under the 
scheme, in order to improve the post -harvest infrastructure facilities and to reduce post -harvest 
losses, financial assistance is provided for setting up of ice plants, cold storages, fish transportation 
vehicles including refrigerated and insulated vehicles, ice/fish holding boxes, etc. Further, 
upgradation of existing fishing vessels for export competency and pro curement of deep sea fishing 
vessels, development of fishing harbours and fish landing centres and modernization of existing 
fishing harbours are supported under this scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

PMGSY-I AND II IN ASSAM 
 
2233.  SHRI KRIPANATH MALLAH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the salient features of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY); 
(b)  the number of projects and roads sanctioned  under PMGSY Phase -I and II in Assam 
during the last three years; 
(c)  the funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized  by the State in this regard during the said 
period; 
(d)  the achievements made so far along with the  details of pending work and the time by 
which the pending work is likely to be completed; and 
(e)  the steps being taken by the Government for  construction of roads to connect the far -
flung areas and the tribal areas of Assam? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)        Rural Roads is a State subject. Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was 
launched as a one-time special intervention to provide rural connectivity, by way of a single 
all-weather road, to the eligible unconnected habitations of designated population size (500+ 
in plain areas and 250+ in North -Eastern States, Himalayan States and Himalayan U nion 
Territories as per 2001 census) in the core network for uplifting the socio-economic condition 
of the rural population. Relaxation has been provided to the Tribal (Schedule V) areas and 
Selected Tribal and Backward Districts (as identified by the Mini stry of Home Affairs 
(MHA) and Planning Commission) and unconnected habitations in these areas with a 
population of 250 persons and above in the Core Network as per Census 2001 are eligible for 
connectivity under the scheme. In the critical Left Wing Extre mism affected blocks (as 
identified by Ministry of Home Affairs), additional relaxation has been given to connect 
habitations with population 100 persons and above as per 2001 census. 
  
The mandate of PMGSY has been subsequently widened to include new inte rventions. 
PMGSY-II was launched in the year 2013, with a target to upgrade 50,000 Kms  of the 
existing rural road network to improve its overall efficiency as a provider of transportation 
services for people, goods and services. Road Connectivity Project f or Left Wing Extremism 
Affected Areas (RCPLWEA) was launched in the year 2016 for construction/ upgradation of 
strategically important roads chosen in the 44 worst affected LWE districts and adjoining 
districts in the 9 States of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chh attisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. PMGSY -III was launched in the year 
2019 for consolidation of 1,25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting 
habitations,  inter-alia, to Gramin Agricultura l Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools 
and Hospitals.  
  
 

 
 
The main features of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) are decentralized and 
evidence based planning, standards and specifications as per Indian Road Congress (IRC) and 
Rural Roads Man ual, dedicated   implementation mechanism at central, state and district 
level, scrutiny of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) at multiple levels, strong IT backbone for 
monitoring and implementation of the programme, three -tier quality management system, 
unbroken flow of funds, inbuilt mechanism for consultation with public representatives in 
planning, selection and monitoring of works, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2236 
  ANSWERED ON 20/12/2022 
 
SPMRM IN TAMIL NADU 
 
2236.  SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI KARUNANIDHI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has any proposal to extend Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban 
Mission (SPMRM); 
(b)  if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c)  the details of funds sanctioned and pending for ongoing projects by the Ministry of 
Rural Development, cluster-wise; and 
(d)  the details of audit/monitoring of outcomes for clusters of Tamil Nadu? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) & (b) There is no proposal to extend Shyama Prasad MukherjiRurban Mission (SPMRM) 
as 31st March 2022 has been declared as the “sunset date” for the scheme by the Government 
of India.  
(c) Under the Mission, funds are not sanctioned but are released to the States/Union 
Territories (UTs). At the first instan ce, an Integrated Cluster Action Plan (ICAP) is prepared 
for a cluster which is approved at the District and the State level. The ICAP is then approved 
by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. After the approval of ICAP, 
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) are approved by the States/Union Territories (UTs) which 
reflect the investment approved for the clusters. The cluster -wise investment as approved for 
283 clusters, as per the Management Information System (MIS) is placed at Annexure 1.  
The Ministry of Rural Development releases only the Critical Gap Fund (CGF) to the 
States/UTs based on the requisition made by the States/UTs and also in accordance with the 
Government of India’s guidelines for release of funds under the Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes. Further releases to clusters are made by the States/UTs. 
 (d)  NITI Aayog undertook an evaluation study on SPMRM covering all States/UTs. The 
study observed that SPMRM growth clusters are playing a role in reducing urban migration 
by ensuring that basic infrastructure and utilities are provided and industrialization is 
promoted. The Mission is very relevant for ensuring transformational development as against 
transitional development in India’s rural development sector. The study also observed that 
SPMRM ensures inter -Ministerial convergence of schemes thereby, ensuring multi -
dimensional benefits. Mission provides clusters the flexibility to choose from 21 components 
which are relevant to the pressing needs of India’s Rurban spaces. Positive improvem ents in 
sanitation, piped water, education, health and road network facilities were also acknowledged 
in the report. 26% of the investment is targeted directly towards economic activities and the 
other investments are also indirectly facilitating the economic growth of the areas.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2237 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 20TH DECEMBER, 2022/AGRAHAYANA 29, 1944 
(SAKA) 
 
SUICIDE BY DAILY WAGERS 
 
2237.  DR. MOHAMMAD JAWED: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that suicide cases of daily  wagers has steadily 
increased in the country since 2014; 
 
(b) if so, the number of such cases of daily  wagers reported in the country 
during the last five years, State-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government is aware that daily  wage earners were the 
largest profession-wise group among suicide victims in 2021; and 
 
(d) the steps are taken by the Government to  prevent suicides by daily 
wagers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c): National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and publishes 
data on suicides in its publication ‘Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 
(ADSI)’. The published reports are available till the year 2021. As per NCRB 
data, State/UT -wise number of suicides committed by daily wage earners 
during 2014-2021 is given at Annexure -I. Profession-wise number of Suicides 
committed by people in the country during 2021 is given at Annexure-II. 
(d): In order to provide social security benefits to the workers in the 
unorganized  sector  including  workers in agriculture sector, the Government  
 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2237 FOR 20.12.2022 
 
has enacted the Unorganized Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008. This Act 
stipulates formulation of  suitable welfare schemes for unorganized workers 
on matters relating to: (i) life and disability cover, (ii) health and maternity 
benefits, (iii) old age protection and (iv) any other benefit as may be 
determined by the Central Government. Life and disabi lity cover is provided 
through Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti BimaYojana (PMJJBY) and Pradhan 
Mantri Suraksha BimaYojana (PMSBY) to the unorganized workers depending 
upon their eligibility. The health and maternity benefits are addressed 
through Ayushman Bhar at scheme. For old age protection in the form of 
minimum assured monthly pension, Government of India has recently 
launched Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM -SYM). Under the 
scheme, which is on contributory basis, minimum assured monthly pension of 
Rs. 3000/- will be provided to the unorganized workers after attaining the age 
of 60 years.

Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
 
(a) whether the Government is having any comparative list of

Olympics are available at website https://olympics.com/en/olympic-

(c) & (d): Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is providing financial 
assistance to recognized National Sports Federations (NSFs) towards 
the training of athletes , which includes all requisite support for their 
preparations, such as Foreign Coaches/supporting staff,  scientific & 
medical support besides financial assistance for their training abroad 
and participation in international competitions in India and abroad 
through the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs . For the said purpose, an 
ACTC (Annual Calendar for Training a nd Competition) budget is 
approved for each NSF every year.  
Further, elite athletes who are medal prospects at mega-sports events, 
including Olympic Games , are supported in a customized mode under 
Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).  
Sports Authority of India (SAI) , an autonomous body under the 
administrative control of the Ministry,  is implementing the following 
Sports Promotional Schemes across the country to identify talented 
sportspersons in various age groups and nurture them to excel at 
national and international levels: 
 National Centres of Excellence (NCOE) 
 SAI Training Centre (STC) 
 Extension Centre of STC 
 National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) 
(its Sub-Schemes - Regular Schools, IGMA & Akharas) 
The selected athletes are supported through expert coaches, sports 
equipment, Scientific support, boarding and lodging, sports kit, 
competition exposure, educational expenses, medical/ insurance, and 
stipend as per the approved scheme norms. 
The government has launched Khelo India Programme with tw in 
objectives of mass participation and the promotion of excellence in 
sports. Various programmes have been established under this scheme 
to promote sports and improve the level of sports and infrastructural 
facilities, including stadiums, playing fields, tracks, and sports training 
in the country at the school level. Under this scheme , various 

initiatives have been undertaken to encourage sportspersons at 
various levels, including those in schools. 
 
So far, under Khelo India Scheme, 733 Khelo India Centres, 29 Khelo 
India State Centres of Excellence and 266 Academies ha ve been 
sanctioned across the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2242 
  ANSWERED ON 20/12/2022 
 
DEFICIENCIES IN PMGSY 
 
2242.  DR. BEESETTI VENKATA SATYAVATHI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken cognizance of the deficiencies in the Pradhan 
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) pointed out by the CAG in its 2016 report in 
terms of data updation on the Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting 
System (OMMAS); 
(b)  if so, the details of measures undertaken; 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d)  the details of proposed measures to be taken 
to make it an effective tool for monitoring and decision making in the implementation 
of PMGSY? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (d)    The deficiencies pointed out by the CAG in its 2016 report in terms of data 
updation on the Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS) have 
been taken care of and as on date, the system has become a robust instrument for monitoring 
various aspects of PMGSY. Over a period of time, various features have been added to make 
it more topical. 
NITI Aayog, in its report “Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in Rural 
Development Sector Vol.2: Rural Development, December 2020”  has also lauded OMMAS 
and other technology initiatives adopted under PMGSY. The observations of NITI Aayog are 
given below:- 
(i) In terms of transparency and level of data, OMMAS is s erving all purposes with 
respect to monitoring. 
(ii) OMMAS has helped facilitate the timely monitoring of works under PMGSY. 
(iii) PMGSY is committed to establish transparency and accountability in the scheme 
processes- through the revamping of its MIS portal (OMMAS) , planning at the Block 
Panchayat, geo -tagging of roads, reporting of the scheme on a monthly basis, and 
timely evaluations. 
(iv) PMGSY has implemented many technology driven mechanisms for planning, 
monitoring, data management, reporting and citizen feedback i ncluding OMMAS,   
Geospatial Rural Road Information System (GRRIS), Geo -PMGSY, Electronic 
Maintenance of Rural Roads under PMGSY (E -MARG) and the Meri Sadak app. All 
of these interventions have improved the efficiency of scheme processes. 
(v) The scheme’s on-track physical progress, a well-defined implementation structure and 
high rates of digitization are promising.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2244 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20/12/2022 
 
Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
 
2244: SHRI P. RAVINDHRANATH: 
 
Will the Minister of Cooperation (सहकाǐरता मंğी) be pleased to state:  
 
a) whether the Government has decided to computerize all Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
(PACS) across the country with the aim to increase efficiency, transparency and 
accountability, if so, the details thereof; 
b) whether the Government has also planned to increase the number of PACSs to cover all 
villages and to ensure credit facility to more number of farmers; and 
c) if so, the details thereof and the actions taken by the Government in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION  
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a): A project for Computerization of 63,000 functional Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
(PACS), with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore has been approved by the Cabinet 
Committee on Economic Affairs vide its decision dated 29th June, 2022. This project entails 
bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common 
software, linking them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District 
Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). Computerization of PACS will provide various benefits 
such as increasing the efficiency of their operations, ensuring speedy disbursal of loans, lowering 
of transaction costs, reducing imbalances in payments, seamless accounting with DCCBs and 
StCBs and increasing transparency. Implementation of Common Accounting System (CAS) and 
Management Information System (MIS) would enable PACS to carry out their operations online 
and obtain refinance/ loans from NABARD through DCCBs and StCBs. 
 
(b) to (c): Yes, Sir. There are nearly 95,000 Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) as 
against 2,55,643 Panchayats and 6,62,750 villages in the country. As per the Allocation of 
Business Rules, 1961, one of the mandates of the Ministry is “Strengthening of cooperative 
movement in the country and deepening its reach up to the grassroots”. Model Byelaws for 
PACS have also been prepared after consultation with various stakeholders including 
States/Union Territories Administration which will allow PACS to diversify their income 
streams, enabling them to avail more credit facilities, in turn benefitting their members, which 
are primarily farmers.

RELIEF TO PILGRIMS OF AMARNATH YATRA 
 
2245.  SHRI RAJAN VICHARE: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of pilgrims who lost their lives  due to flashflood during the 
sacred Amarnath Yatra in July 2022; 
 
(b) whether a number of pilgrims are reported to be missing; 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to  rescue and provide relief to 
pilgrims of Amarnath Yatra? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (d): As per information provided by the Government of Jammu and 
Kashmir, 15 persons l ost their lives due to flashflood but no person has been 
reported missing. Various Government agencies like NDRF, UTDRF, Army, 
CAPFs, UT Govt. Officials and Shri Amarnathji Shrine Board (SASB) Officials 
were deployed for search operations, rescue and relie f of pilgrims. The yatris 
were immediately evacuated to safer places/camps and provided 
accommodation and food while the injured yatris were moved to nearest 
medical facilities. Help line numbers of Joint Control Room Pahalgam, Police 
Control Room Anantnag , SASB and Divisional Commissioner Kashmir were 
circulated on all platforms including social media.

Inland Fisheries and Aquaculture 
2248. SHRI N. REDDEPPA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken  any measures to enhance the contributions by  
considering that in developing countries, contributions  made by inland fisheries and 
aquaculture have the potential of increasing food supplies and alleviating poverty; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)  the details of steps taken by the Government  to increase and improve fisher’s and fish 
farmers’access to adequate te chnical information required to  improve their practices to 
increase production? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) to  (c): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying, Government of India under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) has taken steps to intensify and diversify inland fisheries and aquaculture with focus 
on diversification of species, introduction of new species and peg the critical gaps in the 
demand and supply of quality brood and seed of cultivable species and species-specific feeds, 
Adequate number of brood banks, hatcheries, seed rearing units, specific pathogen free or 
resistant seed, genetically improved brood stock, and feed mills.As a result,Inland fisheries and 
aquaculture has contributed 74.59% of the total fish production of India during 2021 -22.  
Further, the Department of Fisheries under PMMSY is also supporting exposure visits, training 
and capacity building programme  of fish farmers and other stakeholders in modern 
technologies developed in fisheries and aquaculture viz Cage culture in Reservoir, pen culture 
in wetlands, Biofloc Te chnology, Re -circulatory Aquaculture System,  Scaling up of 
Freshwater Prawn (Scampi) Culture, promotion of Inland Saline Aquaculture in potential area 
to improve farm practices for enhanced production.
